newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - AUG 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - AUG 5.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Czech Industry and Transport Association criticized the government yesterday for closing a number of embassies in the developing world. A spokesman for the association said that Czech companies will suffer as a result of the closings since they will not have the necessary support from the government to do business in countries such as Jordan, Latvia, and Yemen.
- Environment Minister Jiri Skalicky said that the most difficult period following flooding in eastern Bohemia and Moravia is now over and that the government is now focussing on repairing damage.

- Petrochemichal giant, Chemopetrol Litvinov a.s. announced profits of 472 million crowns for the first half of 1997. Company officials say that this represents 47 percent of a full-year plan. Sales for the same period were 8.18 billion crowns, which constitues a 2 percent year-on-year increase.

- Konsolidacni banka is lowering its interest rates today by 1 percent to 15.30 percent for newly issued short, medium, and longterm loans. Interest rates on 1 month and 2 month term deposits are also being reduced by 0.40 and 0.60 percent to 11.90 percent and 12.30 percent respectively.

- Finance Minister Ivan Pilip announced yesterday that the government is not willing to increase its 600 million crown subsidy for the upcoming IMF-World Bank forum scheduled for the year 2000. 350 million crowns have been set asside in the state budget, while another 250 million crowns will be provided by the Czech National Bank.
- Slovakia plans to continue imposing a 7 percent import deposit adopted on 21 July.
- Despite showroom price increases Skoda Felicias made by Skoda Mlada Boleslav are still 3.2 percent cheaper than their nearest competition on the Czech market.

- Financial results for leasing companies will be affected this year by damage from flooding, the decline in the value of the crown, and fluctuations in interest rates. Leasing firms are offering clients affected by flooding a postponement on payments.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - The demand for foreign currency declined in June as confidence of Czechs in the crown increased. There was a massive rush in May as Czechs lined up to change their crowns for dollars, D-marks, and other Western currencies when the CNB allowed the crown to float freely on international money markets.

- The government will provide 265 million crowns in direct assistance to energy companies affected by flooding. Five companies hit worst by the flooding will receive 5-year interest-free loans according to Industry and trade Minister Karel Kuhnl.

LIDOVE NOVINY - The Czech Republic increased its foreign currency reserves to $15.041 which represents an increase of $556 million from May. In June, CNB foreign currency reserves reached $10.764 billion, while in May they fell to $ 10.025 billion.

- The regional commercial court in Prague ruled yesterday to allow minority shareholders represented by Trend to take control of Kotva department store, thus ending a period when two entities controlled the activities of the store.

PRAVO - Seven companies, including Bohemia Sekt and B-Prit are battling to take control of 89 percent of Becherovka karlovy Vary. The bidders are prepared to pay between 1-2 billion crowns for the Czech liquor maker.
